problems.title: Add Two Numbers
problems.description:
Return the sum of the two whole numbers `a` and `b`.

This is the smallest possible problem: it checks that you can write a function that **returns** a value instead of printing it.
hints: Functions send results back with return.
Use the + operator.
return a + b

solutions.python:
def add_numbers(a, b):
    return a + b

problems.title: Even or Odd
problems.description: Given a whole number `n`, return the string `"Even"` if it is divisible by 2, otherwise `"Odd"`.
hints: The remainder operator % tells you what is left after dividing.
n % 2 is 0 for even numbers.
if n % 2 == 0: return "Even" else return "Odd"

solutions.python:
def even_or_odd(n):
    return "Even" if n % 2 == 0 else "Odd"

problems.title: Largest of Three
problems.description: Return the largest of the three numbers `a`, `b` and `c`. Try writing it with `if` statements before reaching for a built-in.
hints: Keep a variable holding the biggest value seen so far.
Start with a, then compare with b and c.
best = a; if b > best: best = b; if c > best: best = c

problems.title: Sum of a List
problems.description:
Return the sum of all numbers in the list `nums`. An empty list sums to 0.

Write it with a loop and a running total, the way you would explain it in an interview.
hints: Start a total at 0.
Loop over the list and add each number.
for n in nums: total += n

problems.title: Count the Vowels
problems.description: Return how many vowels (`a`, `e`, `i`, `o`, `u`, in lower or upper case) appear in the string `s`.
constraints: s contains English letters, spaces and punctuation
hints: Look at the string one character at a time.
Lower-case each character before checking.
if ch.lower() in "aeiou": count += 1

problems.title: Reverse a String
hints: Build a new string by visiting characters from the end.
In Python, slicing with a step of -1 reverses: s[::-1].
Or loop: result = ch + result for every character.

problems.title: FizzBuzz
problems.description:
Return a list of strings for the numbers 1 to `n`. For multiples of 3 use `"Fizz"`, for multiples of 5 use `"Buzz"`, for multiples of both use `"FizzBuzz"`, and otherwise the number itself as a string.

A classic screening question: it tests loops, conditions and the order of your checks.

examples.explanation: 15 is a multiple of both 3 and 5

hints: Loop from 1 to n.
Check 'multiple of 15' before the separate 3 and 5 checks.
i % 15 == 0 -> FizzBuzz, elif i % 3 == 0 -> Fizz, elif i % 5 == 0 -> Buzz, else str(i)

problems.title: Largest Number in a List
problems.description: Return the largest number in the non-empty list `nums` **without** using the built-in `max`. Walking the list yourself is the point of the exercise.
hints: Remember the biggest value seen so far.
Start with the first element, not 0 (numbers can be negative).
for n in nums: if n > best: best = n

problems.title: Count Positive Numbers
problems.description: Return how many numbers in `nums` are strictly greater than zero.
hints: Use a counter that starts at 0.
Zero is not positive.
if n > 0: count += 1

problems.title: Palindrome Word
problems.description: A palindrome reads the same forwards and backwards, like `"level"`. Given a lower-case word `s`, return `true` if it is a palindrome and `false` otherwise.
hints: Compare the word with its reverse.
Or compare the first and last letters, then move inwards.
return s == s[::-1]

problems.title: Factorial
problems.description: The factorial of `n` (written n!) is `1 x 2 x 3 x ... x n`, and `0!` is defined as `1`. Return `n!`.
hints: Start a result at 1, not 0.
Multiply by every number from 1 to n.
for i in range(1, n + 1): result *= i

problems.title: Multiplication Table
problems.description: Return a list of the first 10 multiples of `n`: `[n x 1, n x 2, ..., n x 10]`.
hints: Loop i from 1 to 10.
Append n * i to a list each time.
[n * i for i in range(1, 11)]

solutions.python:
def multiplication_table(n):
    return [n * i for i in range(1, 11)]

problems.title: Letter Grade
problems.description: Convert an exam `score` from 0 to 100 into a letter: 90 and above is `"A"`, 80-89 `"B"`, 70-79 `"C"`, 60-69 `"D"`, and below 60 `"F"`.
hints: Check the highest band first.
Use if / elif / else so only one branch runs.
if score >= 90: return 'A' elif score >= 80: ...

problems.title: Count Words
problems.description: A sentence `s` contains words separated by single spaces, with no spaces at the start or end. Return the number of words. An empty string has 0 words.
hints: Every space separates two words.
Handle the empty string first.
Split on spaces and count the pieces, or count spaces + 1.

problems.title: Sum of Digits
problems.description: Return the sum of the digits of the non-negative whole number `n`. For example `472` gives `4 + 7 + 2 = 13`.
problems.complexity: O(number of digits) time, O(1) space
hints: n % 10 gives the last digit.
n // 10 removes the last digit.
while n > 0: total += n % 10; n //= 10

problems.title: Leap Year
problems.description: Return `true` if `year` is a leap year. A year is a leap year if it is divisible by 4, **except** years divisible by 100, which are leap years only if they are also divisible by 400.
hints: Turn each rule into a condition with %.
Check 400 first, then 100, then 4.
return year % 400 == 0 or (year % 4 == 0 and year % 100 != 0)

solutions.python:
def leap_year(year):
    return year % 400 == 0 or (year % 4 == 0 and year % 100 != 0)
